1.title: 11 Grok Bots I Still Use Every Day (Steal These Now)
1.author: Peter Yang
1.hook: Walk-through of 11 specialized bots (email delegation, content research, fitness tracking, advisor) that coordinate as a system, with the brutally-honest-advisor prompt included.

2.title: How SpaceXAI designers use Grok Bot and Figma MCP to ship faster
2.author: How I AI
2.hook: Two designers at xAI share concrete workflows—voice memos to Figma via MCP, self-updating websites via Grok Bot backend, shower-thought-to-prototype loops—showing how agents replace traditional design handoffs.

3.title: Tokens Should Have Jobs — Katelyn Lesse & Angela Jiang, Anthropic 2026-09-14 16:00
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Agent architecture patterns that trade token allocation (advise/grade/dream strategies) for better reliability on tasks where 80% accuracy is useless — with benchmarked tradeoffs between single-run success and token efficiency.

1.title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Agent orchestration moves from client-side Python loops to server-side sandboxes with credential injection and domain allowlists, shrinking harness code as model capability increases.

2.title: How we Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Chief of Software at Vercel walks through three iterations of an internal data agent (mega prompt → scoped agent chain → single agent with state management), with eval score doubling after switching to file system conventions instead of custom tools.

3.title: No Memory, No Harness: Why the Database Is the Last Line of Defense — Kay Malcolm, Oracle
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: A senior PM at Oracle walks through five types of memory systems (short-term, long-term, episodic, procedural, semantic) for AI agents and argues the database choice is a team productivity multiplier, not just a technical detail—demonstrated with a live experiment showing how four different stores create reconciliation overhead.

1.title: Every step you take, every call you make: the reliable agent stack — Giselle van Dongen, Restate
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Durable execution infrastructure for agents — journal-based recovery that replays to exact failure point, virtual objects for session isolation, mid-flight cancellation and signaling of live agent loops.

2.title: Loophole: Adversarial Agents To Stress Test Your Morality — Brendan Rappazzo, Morgan Stanley
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Multi-agent system that translates moral principles into formal code, then uses adversarial agents to surface loopholes (legal-but-immoral) and overreach (moral-but-illegal), with concrete branches: chatbot constitutions, contract validation, and a Senate simulator that hill-climbs bills toward passage.

3.title: We let an AI agent execute Bash and lived to talk about it — Sarah Sanders, PostHog
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Security audit of an agentic CLI (PostHog's Wizard) that executes bash commands at scale, revealing how attacks compose across innocent-looking layers and how to detect them without enforcement.
